newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced smartly in early Monday morning trade, recovering some of the previous week's losses, while trading of index futures was also active, brokers said.
However, the rebound came chiefly on the back of a jump in HSBC Holdings, brokers added.
"The big players have covered their positions in the futures market after driving Hongkong Bank down last week," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index put on 125 points to 13,238, thus edging back above the key support level of 13,200.
Early Monday turnover rose to a healthy HK$1.1 billion.
The February Hang Seng Index futures contract gained only 83 to 13,223, still moving at a cautious discount to the cash market although trading was brisk, analysts said.
International banking giant HSBC Holdings put on HK$2.50 to HK$186.00 on thin volume of only HK$90.95 million.
The sharp drop last week had investors and analysts concerned.
"If the index holds above 12,700, its major support level and previous long-term resistance level, the uptrend will remain intact," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
"The second quarter (of this year) will be much better," Cheung said.

But Cheung added that the market would need to see heavy turnover to push it through the 13,500 resistance level, and that range trading below this level was more likely in advance of the reporting season.
Hang Seng Index constituents reporting results soon are Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels on Wednesday and Hong Kong and China Gas on February 27.
The luxury hotel counter gained HK$0.15 to HK$13.80, while China Gas added HK$0.05 to HK$14.45.
Conglomerate Swire Pacific was among the most actively traded, gaining HK$0.25 to HK$65.50. The share was sharply sold down last Friday.
Cheung Kong was the most active property counter, rising HK$0.50 to HK$72.25.
